Inclusive playground opens for kids of all abilities in Overland Park

By Claire Decatur
Published: Oct. 13, 2026 at 6:35 PM EDT
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:32
Instaread

OVERLAND PARK, Kan. (KCTV) - A new playground designed for children of all abilities officially opened Tuesday at the Blue Valley Sports Complex.

Brody’s Boundless Playground was unveiled through a partnership between Blue Valley Recreation, Variety KC, the Michael & Brandy Rea Family Foundation and community partners. The playground features accessible equipment and sensory-friendly spaces designed so children can walk, roll, climb, swing and explore together.

Sensory-friendly soft opening

The day began with a sensory-friendly soft opening from 2 to 3:30 p.m., reserved for Variety KC families. The smaller gathering allowed children to experience the playground with fewer people, less noise and a calmer environment before the public event.

An official ribbon-cutting ceremony followed at 4 p.m., with a community play day running from 4:15 to 6 p.m. Chick-fil-A, Kona Ice, The Golden Scoop, Scheels and other community partners were on-site for the celebration.

Playground designed with accessibility in mind

According to Variety KC, less than 20% of all parks have accessibility features. The playground took three years to design and build.

Marc Harrell, CEO of Variety KC, said skills like negotiating, communicating and taking turns are often learned on the playground rather than in the classroom.

“You learn how to negotiate on the playground, you learn how to communicate with others, you learn how to be friends, challenge, wait your turn,” Harrell said. “All of those skills aren’t taught in a classroom; it was at recess or on a playground.”

Lezlie John, a mother of four, said the playground gives her daughter Tatum more independence.

“We love the opportunity for her to walk all the way to the top,” John said. “She also enjoys swings. A lot of times she has to be put in or harnessed into a swing, and there’s not that many usually at parks.”

Melissa Sabin, whose son Logan attended the opening, said he was drawn to one piece of equipment in particular.

“His favorite — and I don’t know what it’s called — but the slide that has all the rolls,” Sabin said. “There’s something about the sensory input of that that he loves.”

Sabin said watching Logan play without added worry stood out to her.

“Just to see him smile and having fun and not having to worry if he’s going to fall off something is so incredibly important,” Sabin said.

The playground is named in honor of Brody Rea, whose parents, Michael and Brandy Rea, founded the Michael & Brandy Rea Family Foundation.
